PLANT-LEVEL DRIVER (Operating Segment Information, p.7-8): VPEL operates four generation assets -- Erathna MHP and Denawaka Ganga MHP (mini-hydro), Kiriwaneliya MHP (mini-hydro), and the newly-commissioned Dolahena GMSP (Ground-Mounted Solar PV; 'Nil' generation/revenue in the Q1 FY2025/26 comparative, confirming it was not yet operating a year ago). Total Group generation rose to 29,961 MWh from 26,754 MWh (+12.0% YoY), but this was driven entirely by Dolahena's first-time contribution of 4,653 MWh / Rs.118,553k revenue -- the three existing hydro plants' combined generation actually fell slightly (15,004+7,710+4,040=26,754 MWh PY vs 13,328+7,726+4,254=25,308 MWh this quarter, -5.4%), with Erathna MHP specifically down 11.2% (15,004 to 13,328 MWh) driving most of the hydro-fleet decline -- consistent with a weaker hydrology/rainfall year at that catchment, though the filing itself gives no explicit rainfall commentary (a gap). Ex-Dolahena, Group revenue would have been essentially flat to slightly down YoY (Rs.416,828k vs Rs.424,138k, -1.7%) -- effectively all of the reported +26.2% Group revenue growth is attributable to the new solar plant. Finance Cost surged from Rs.(1,006,514) to Rs.(36,376,394) (36x YoY) as Interest Bearing Borrowings jumped to Rs.1,176,000,000 non-current + Rs.196,000,000 current (from a much smaller base) to fund the Dolahena project -- interest was likely capitalized into Capital Work-in-Progress during last year's construction phase and only started hitting the P&L as a financing expense once the plant was commissioned, consistent with Capex (Acquisitions of PPE) falling sharply from Rs.(753,614,139) in Q1 FY2025/26 (construction phase) to Rs.(26,072,631) this quarter (post-commissioning). No foreign-currency-denominated debt or FX exposure is disclosed for VPEL -- all borrowings and the one contingent liability (Rs.651,700,000 in bank guarantees to Sri Lanka Customs for the Dolahena bonding-warehouse import facility) are LKR-denominated; FX risk does not appear to be a material factor for this filing.

interim_updates.note_text: Vallibel Power Erathna PLC (VPEL) reported Group Revenue of Rs.535,382,758 for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), +26.2% YoY (2025: Rs.424,139,185), Profit Before Tax of Rs.374,463,489, +11.5% YoY (2025: Rs.335,785,017), and Net Profit of Rs.301,252,174, +12.4% YoY (2025: Rs.268,007,017). [Note: all VPEL figures in this entry are in ABSOLUTE Rupees, not Rs.'000, per the source filing.] By plant (Operating Segment Information, p.7-8): the newly-commissioned Dolahena Ground-Mounted Solar PV Plant (GMSP) generated 4,653 MWh and Rs.118,553,000 of revenue this quarter -- it generated Nil in the Q1 FY2025/26 comparative, confirming it was not yet operating a year ago. Group generation volume rose to 29,961 MWh from 26,754 MWh (+12.0% YoY), but this headline increase is driven entirely by Dolahena: the three pre-existing mini-hydro plants' COMBINED generation actually FELL 5.4% YoY, from 26,754 MWh to 25,308 MWh. Erathna MHP specifically fell 11.2% (13,328 MWh vs 15,004 MWh PY) with revenue down 8.5% to Rs.111,294,000 (2025: Rs.121,681,000) -- consistent with weaker hydrology/river flow at that catchment this quarter, though the filing itself gives no explicit rainfall commentary. Denawaka Ganga MHP was essentially flat (generation +0.2% to 7,726 MWh, revenue -0.3% to Rs.198,226,000), and Kiriwaneliya MHP grew modestly (generation +5.3% to 4,254 MWh, revenue +3.6% to Rs.107,308,000). Excluding Dolahena, Group revenue from the legacy hydro fleet was roughly flat to slightly down YoY (Rs.416,828,000 vs Rs.424,138,000 combined, -1.7%) -- effectively all of the Group's +26.2% headline revenue growth, and all Rs.77,180,000 of the increase, is attributable to the new solar plant. Dolahena also carried a strong 79.6% gross margin in its first comparable quarter (Gross Profit Rs.90,913,000 on Rs.118,553,000 revenue). Below Gross Profit, Finance Cost surged 36x YoY to Rs.(36,376,394) from just Rs.(1,006,514) PY, as Interest Bearing Borrowings used to fund the Dolahena project (Rs.1,176,000,000 non-current + Rs.196,000,000 current at 30 June 2026) began hitting the P&L as a financing expense rather than being capitalized into Capital Work-in-Progress during construction -- consistent with Capex (Acquisitions of PPE) falling sharply to Rs.(26,072,631) this quarter from Rs.(753,614,139) in Q1 FY2025/26 (the peak construction period). PBT growth (+11.5%) still trailed Gross Profit growth (+20.5%, to Rs.454,489,187 from Rs.377,309,688) because of this finance-cost drag. No foreign-currency debt or FX exposure is disclosed -- all borrowings and the one contingent liability (Rs.651,700,000 in bank guarantees to Sri Lanka Customs for the Dolahena bonding-warehouse import facility) are LKR-denominated.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is VPEL's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter previously stored; the most recent prior manual documents registered for VPEL were Annual Reports, not interim filings). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) no explicit rainfall/hydrology commentary is given despite Erathna MHP's 11.2% YoY generation decline -- the filing discloses generation volumes but not a stated cause; (2) the filing does not disclose forward guidance on when the Dolahena solar plant reached full commissioning, nor its expected steady-state generation/revenue run-rate; (3) Country Energy (Private) Limited is consolidated as VPEL's sole subsidiary (Note 3) but its standalone financial contribution is not separately broken out anywhere in this filing, only inferable from the Group-vs-Company column differences; (4) no sensitivity or hedging disclosure is given for the Rs.1,372,000,000 combined interest-bearing borrowings (all appear to be floating/local-currency, but the specific interest rate basis is not stated in this filing).
interim_updates.takeaway: VPEL's headline growth this quarter (Revenue +26.2%, PAT +12.4%) is a single-asset story: the newly-commissioned Dolahena solar plant contributed Rs.118,553,000 of revenue at a strong 79.6% gross margin in its first comparable quarter, while the pre-existing hydro fleet's combined revenue was roughly flat to slightly down (-1.7%), with Erathna MHP's generation down 11.2% likely reflecting weaker hydrology (unstated in the filing). The debt used to build Dolahena is now flowing through the P&L as finance cost (up 36x YoY) rather than being capitalized as before, which is why profit growth (PBT +11.5%, PAT +12.4%) trailed revenue and gross-profit growth (+26.2% / +20.5%) -- a normal and expected pattern for a plant moving from construction to steady-state operation, not a sign of operating weakness.

operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.535,382,758, +26.2% YoY (2025: Rs.424,139,185); PBT Rs.374,463,489, +11.5% YoY; Net Profit Rs.301,252,174, +12.4% YoY. [Figures in absolute Rupees, not Rs.'000.]

Newly-commissioned Dolahena solar plant (GMSP) generated 4,653 MWh / Rs.118,553,000 revenue this quarter (Nil in the year-ago comparative) at a 79.6% gross margin -- this single new asset accounts for effectively all of the Group's revenue growth.

The three pre-existing mini-hydro plants' combined generation FELL 5.4% YoY (26,754 to 25,308 MWh); Erathna MHP specifically fell 11.2% (15,004 to 13,328 MWh), consistent with weaker hydrology at that catchment, though not explicitly stated in the filing.
Excluding Dolahena, legacy hydro-fleet revenue was roughly flat to down YoY (-1.7%, Rs.416,828,000 vs Rs.424,138,000).

Finance Cost surged 36x YoY to Rs.(36,376,394) as Dolahena's construction debt (Rs.1,176mn long-term + Rs.196mn short-term borrowings) began hitting the P&L post-commissioning; Capex fell to Rs.(26,072,631) this quarter from Rs.(753,614,139) a year earlier as the project moved from construction to operations.
key_drivers: The newly-commissioned Dolahena solar plant (Rs.118,553,000 revenue, Rs.90,913,000 Gross Profit, 79.6% margin, Nil in the prior-year comparative) is responsible for essentially all of the Group's headline revenue (+26.2%) and Gross Profit (+20.5%) growth this quarter.

Erathna MHP generation fell 11.2% YoY (15,004 to 13,328 MWh), the largest driver of a 5.4% combined decline across the three legacy hydro plants -- consistent with weaker hydrology, though the filing does not explicitly attribute it to rainfall.

Finance Cost surged 36x YoY (to Rs.36,376,394) as debt used to fund Dolahena's construction began hitting the P&L post-commissioning rather than being capitalized -- this caused PBT growth (+11.5%) to trail Gross Profit growth (+20.5%).
